CENTRAL BANK OF BELIZE
Belize
The Central Bank of Belize issues the Belize dollar, held at a fixed rate to the US dollar. In August 2021 governor Gustavo Manuel Vasquez lost his post. Prime Minister John Briceno said the board had recommended he resign because of a lot of policy differences. Vasquez wrote that his appointment was terminated on the instructions of the Ministry of Finance, that he faced opposition from it, and that he had tried to restore the bank's integrity and operational autonomy. Castillo Sanchez & Burrell, LLP, Chartered Accountants audited the 2013 accounts, and De La Rue printed the new 100-dollar note introduced on 4 August 2025. Belize scores 32 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and it tells the public little, 4 of 15 on a transparency measure in 2019. Two career moves are recorded, both out of the bank and back into it. The Central Bank of Belize's own Office of the Governor page gives Kareem Michael as Monetary Economist in 2000 and Deputy Director of Research in 2008, says he resigned in 2014 to become Senior Business Analyst at Belize Electricity Limited, and records him returning as Deputy Governor in November 2017, Acting Governor on 13 August 2021 and Governor on 1 December 2021. Who owns Belize Electricity Limited is not stated there, and it is a utility rather than a financial firm. The second move does run through private finance, in the bank's own words: the same page says Deputy Governor Marina Laetitia Murillo joined the bank as a research officer in August 1991, worked from 1998 in project management in the non-government sector and in management positions in the private financial sector, and returned in November 2011 as Economist I, becoming assistant manager of the financial system development unit in October 2018 and Deputy Governor on 1 September 2022. The firms are not named. Moving between jobs is not wrongdoing.

BANK OF BOTSWANA
Botswana
The Bank of Botswana issues the pula, which it manages against the South African rand, moving the rate in small steps within a narrow band. One case is recorded and it ended in acquittal. A woman arrested on 17 October 2019 was accused, with others including former president Ian Khama and former intelligence head Isaac Kgosi, of stealing 100 billion pula from the bank. High Court judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated and referred the investigator to police for perjury prosecution. The accusations against the others remain unproven. One career move is documented: Linah Kelebogile Mohohlo joined the bank on 20 April 1976, worked at the International Monetary Fund from 1994 to 1996 under its Special Appointee Programme, in the African Department and the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, and later served as the bank's Governor and Chairman of the Board from 20 October 1999 until she retired in October 2016, having earlier been Deputy Governor and the founding director of its foreign department. Northern Trust works for the bank on measuring and explaining how its investments have performed and on training staff, which the source describes as reporting and training rather than management of its assets. The 10 pula polymer note that entered circulation on 1 February 2018 was designed and printed by De La Rue. EY audits the accounts. Botswana scores 23 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.

BANK OF LITHUANIA
Lithuania

NATIONAL BANK OF THE REPUBLIC OF NORTH MACEDONIA
North Macedonia
North Macedonia's money is the denar, issued by the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia and held in practice at a fixed rate to the euro. It scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and its weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it. Its notes are printed abroad, by three firms in turn. The bank contracted the French firm Oberthur Fiduciaire to print 100-denar notes, reported on 8 May 2026, for 59,800,000 denars, about 972,358 euros. It had contracted the Russian state company Goznak for the 100-denar notes in 2021, for about 400,000 euros, as part of a 2.2 million euro reissue carrying the state's changed constitutional name. Three separate contracts with De La Rue International cover the 10, 500 and 1,000 denar notes, 45 million notes for 3.775 million euros in total, 20 million of them polymer. One case is recorded, running from 2017 to 2020, and it is unproven: an association of depositors of Eurostandard Bank said in a press release that the governor tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was put under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so it could keep operating. The association said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted, and that over 60 million euros were lost; no charges and no official finding are reported. The European Central Bank gave the bank a temporary line to borrow euros against collateral from 15 December 2022 to 15 January 2024, which has expired. One career move is on record and it too stays outside the private sector, so it is listed but not counted: governor Anita Angelovska Bezhoska spent about eight years at the Ministry of Finance, ending as manager of the treasury department, and was state secretary in 2003 and 2004, then worked as an economist at the International Monetary Fund in Washington before joining the bank as chief economist, serving almost eight years as vice-governor and becoming governor in May 2018. The page the bank publishes names no private firm and no commercial bank. Its books are checked from outside by Grant Thornton DOO of Skopje, which signed the independent auditor's report on the bank's 2023 financial statements and gave an opinion without qualifications; the bank publishes that report on its own site and in the Official Gazette.
